title: Northwind reliability, January to September 2026
brief: Northwind Utilities must report electric reliability for January to September 2026 to the state regulator and to its own board, and the reliability engineer, Sven Lindqvist, wants a data summary page. The system serves 412000 customers. The average outage time per customer so far this year is 99.6 minutes, against a regulator target of 105 for the period. By district, with customers, outage events and average outage minutes per customer: Coastal, 98000, 41, 112; Valley, 142000, 58, 84; Hills, 61000, 37, 176; Metro, 87000, 22, 49; Plains, 24000, 19, 131. That is 177 outage events in all. The system as a whole meets the target, but Hills (176), Plains (131) and Coastal (112) are each above 105, and Hills is the worst by a wide margin. Causes of outage minutes: storms 46 percent, equipment failure 27, vegetation 15, other 12. Mention that a tree-trimming program in Hills was approved to start on 2026-11-02 with a budget of 1.8 million dollars, covering 210 line miles, and that Metro's low figure reflects its underground cables. Sections: "Reliability at a glance", "By district", "Causes" and "Next steps". Make sure the district comparison shows both the biggest districts and the worst performers, and that readers can see which districts are above the 105 target.

edit.request: Hills was corrected to 160 average outage minutes after a data check, which brings the system average to 97.3 minutes.
